$description:
Mode-independent tokens, mirroring shadcn/ui's own theme. DTCG 2025.10. Source of truth — emits src/styles/tokens.css + src/tokens.ts via `npm run tokens`. Never hand-write a CSS variable.

Only what shadcn defines lives here. Inter is the system sans face; named type roles remain Tailwind utility mappings until the typography lab promotes them to authored tokens. Spacing, opacity, breakpoints and shadows are Tailwind defaults and need no token until something actually demands one. A type role consumed by a ported component holds shadcn's shipped value; a role nothing consumes yet holds the authored ideal. Changing a consumed value is a deliberate act that gets its own commit and its own screenshot diff — never a drive-by edit.

Every `lineHeight` inside a `type-*` typography composite is authored in px, never as a unitless ratio: a ratio has to be multiplied by a font size, and tooling reading the token has none in hand — the composite's own fontSize sub-property is a sibling value, not something a lineHeight entry can reach across and multiply. That rule governs roles, full stop, because a role is defined by setting its own font size.

Issue 07b (line-height axis): the `leading-*` tokens below are the stated exception, not a repeal. They exist for elements that override line-height without owning a full type role of their own — which, in src/ui today, is two cases, not one. In the first, the element's size is inherited from a parent (leading-flush's card/chart/calendar consumers, leading-grouped's attachment, leading-clustered's two field slots): no font size is known at authoring time, so a unitless ratio is not a workaround, it is the only form the value can take at all. In the second, the element carries a type role for its size but deliberately takes a line-height that is not the role's — leading-prose's two consumers, empty.tsx EmptyDescription and bubble.tsx BubbleContent, apply leading-prose (1.625, i.e. 22.75px) over the text-body role, whose own line-height is 20px, to give loose prose a rhythm the role does not. For this second case a font size IS known, so px would be expressible; the unitless ratio is chosen for one namespace and one shape across the whole axis, not forced by an unknown size. That is the boundary Issue 07h drew after an audit found this paragraph read as if every consumer were the first case: the 'size unknown, so unitless is the only option' argument covers the six inherited-size consumers, not empty and bubble. Each is named for the job it does (the same convention the type-* roles use), never for a position on a ladder, and is mapped straight into Tailwind's --leading-* namespace in src/styles/system.css — one utility, one token, the same shape --text-* gives the roles. A leading-* token with no consumer in src/ui is not added speculatively; see each token's own $description for its consumer(s).

Issue 07c (density — authored, not yet rewired): `control-height-*` is Button's own height ladder (xs/sm/default/lg), confirmed against Tailwind 4's installed `--spacing-<name>` mechanism rather than assumed from memory — a named key in that namespace generates `h-<name>`, `size-<name>`, `px-<name>`, `py-<name>` and their `has-[>svg]:` compounds alike, so one token backs a control's height and its icon-only square at once. This batch authors the full ladder and rewires exactly Button and Input, the two clearest consumers; the rest of src/ui keeps its raw utilities at the same pixel values until rewired component-by-component, the way the type roles were. Container padding and the 9-step gap scale surveyed alongside this ladder are deliberately left untokenized — they are Tailwind's own scale showing through, not a naming job, and a token authored with no wired consumer this commit is not added speculatively. `control-height-*` genuinely is the shared job "be an N-height box" everywhere it recurs (see the survey note on each height token), so a single name serving many components is correct there.

Issue 07d (density — two layers, replacing 07c's single-layer padding names): 07c named its padding tokens after Button's own variant slots (`control-padding-x-xs`, etc.) and then listed foreign, unrewired consumers — toggle.tsx, badge.tsx, command.tsx and others — in the same token's own $description. That is the defect the type axis already solved by splitting into two layers: a `font-size-*` primitive named for its raw value, referenced from nowhere but this file, and a `type-*` role named for its job, the only thing a component consumes. Density's padding values get the identical split. `padding-{4,6,8,10,12,16}` below are primitives, named for their px value the way `font-size-14` is, holding no opinion about who uses them and consumed by nothing outside this file. `button-padding-*` and `input-padding-*` are the semantics — one per real job in Button's own recipe and Input's own recipe respectively — each pointing at a primitive via a `{name}` alias. Button's sm slot and Input's own horizontal padding happen to share the 12px primitive today; they are still two separate semantics, because they are two different jobs that may diverge, the same reason `type-body-strong` and `type-control` stay separate despite being the same four values. When a future issue rewires another component (toggle.tsx, badge.tsx, ...), it gets a semantic naming *that* component's job — reusing an existing primitive if the number matches, never reusing another component's semantic just because the number is convenient. The foreign-file survey that 07c's token descriptions used to carry is recorded below, against each primitive, as a survey note rather than as a description of any one semantic's job — useful for the next rewire to know which primitive already has the right number, not a claim that those files are wired today.

Survey notes, primitive by value (none of the following files are wired to a token this commit): 6px also appears in toggle.tsx (sm), attachment.tsx, bubble.tsx, combobox.tsx, rail-sidebar.tsx. 8px also appears in badge.tsx, command.tsx, menubar.tsx, sidebar.tsx, tabs.tsx (18 files total — the most-repeated horizontal control padding in src/ui) and, on the vertical axis, is not otherwise surveyed beyond Button's own default. 10px also appears in toggle.tsx (lg), attachment.tsx, chart.tsx, input-group.tsx, pagination.tsx, sidebar.tsx. 12px also appears in command.tsx, native-select.tsx, select.tsx, textarea.tsx, tooltip.tsx. 16px also appears in button-group.tsx, item.tsx, navigation-menu.tsx (trigger — an exact height+padding match for Button's default recipe). 4px also appears widely as a menu/list item's own vertical padding (context-menu.tsx, dropdown-menu.tsx, menubar.tsx, select.tsx, native-select.tsx data-[size=sm]).

Issue 07e (density — two families rewired, per-component vs per-job settled): badge.tsx, toggle.tsx and kbd.tsx ("small pill controls") and dropdown-menu.tsx, context-menu.tsx and menubar.tsx ("menus") were rewired to test whether padding scales per-component, the way 07d's four semantics were named, or per-job, the way `control-height-*` already is. The hard stop 07d set — never author a third semantic pointing at one primitive — was tripped repeatedly, and the outcome answers the question directly.

padding-8 was already at its two-semantic cap (button-padding-x-xs, button-padding-y-default) and stayed there. Four more genuinely distinct jobs wanted this primitive's 8px value and none were authored: badge.tsx's own content-sized pill inset (no height, no icon-conditional pairing, unlike Button's own xs slot); toggle.tsx's default-size unconditional inset (36px-height-paired, unlike Button's icon-conditional xs slot); the menu row's own horizontal inset, identical across dropdown-menu.tsx/context-menu.tsx/menubar.tsx's Item/CheckboxItem/RadioItem/Label/SubTrigger; and menubar.tsx's own MenubarTrigger toolbar-row inset. All four remain raw `px-2`/`pr-2` in source.

padding-6 had one existing semantic (button-padding-x-icon-xs) and room for exactly one more. Two genuinely different jobs competed for it: the menu row's own vertical inset (shared, byte-identical, across all three menu files' Item/CheckboxItem/RadioItem/Label/SubTrigger — the strongest multi-file job evidence found this batch, chosen, now `menu-item-padding-y`) and toggle.tsx's sm-size unconditional inset (single-file, lost the slot, stays raw `px-1.5`, reported as hard-stop-blocked).

padding-4 had one existing semantic (input-padding-y) and room for one more. Two single-file candidates competed: kbd.tsx's own horizontal inset (a different CSS axis from input-padding-y's vertical job, an unambiguous second job, chosen, now `kbd-padding-x`) and menubar.tsx's MenubarTrigger vertical inset (stays raw `py-1`, reported as hard-stop-blocked — would have been the third).

padding-10 had one existing semantic (button-padding-x-icon-sm) and exactly one genuine candidate: toggle.tsx's lg-size unconditional inset, unconditional and 40px-height-paired unlike Button's icon-conditional sm slot. No conflict; added as `toggle-padding-x-lg`.

Heights are the control case the task asked for, and none resisted: every 32/36/40px box in these six files (toggle.tsx's three size variants, menubar.tsx's own root) now consumes the matching `control-height-*` ladder tier directly — no new semantic needed, because the ladder was already named for the job, not for Button. The only height anomaly is kbd.tsx's own `h-5`/`min-w-5` (20px), which was never a ladder candidate — it matches none of the four rungs, forcing it onto `control-height-xs` (24px) would silently change the rendered pixel, and it stays raw with a single consumer. badge.tsx's own `py-0.5` (2px) is likewise a new value with no primitive and one consumer — reported, not authored, matching the one-consumer rule already established for calendar.tsx's p-3 and command.tsx's h-12.

No renames were made this issue. Every reuse here (the four height slots) was already against a job-named token that never carried a component's name to begin with; no padding candidate turned out to share a structural job with an existing per-component semantic closely enough to justify renaming it — 8px's four blocked candidates in particular differ from button-padding-x-xs/button-padding-y-default by conditionality, height-pairing or fixed-vs-content sizing, not merely by which file uses them.

Verdict: padding is per-job, the same as height, but a shared raw pixel value is not itself evidence of a shared job — each candidate was decided on whether its icon-conditionality, height-pairing and fixed-vs-content sizing actually matched an existing consumer, not on whether the number matched. Height's four jobs turned out to already be shared everywhere they recur because "be an N-height box" really is one job irrespective of component; padding's jobs multiply faster, because a control's own padding recipe is shaped by more than its size tier, so most of the 8px/6px/4px collisions surveyed in 07d turned out to be coincidence, not a shared name — the one padding job that did prove genuinely shared across files (menu-item-padding-y) was found the same way control-height-* was, by checking whether every consumer is structurally the same thing, not by grepping for a matching number.

Issue 07f (density — the per-primitive cap was wrong, replaced by a description test): 07e's own hard stop — never author a third semantic pointing at one primitive — was a defect, not a safeguard. It fired four times on padding-8, the single most-repeated inline padding value in the library, and every one of the four candidates it blocked was already an adjudicated, structurally distinct job under 07e's own method: badge.tsx's content-sized pill inset, toggle.tsx's default-size unconditional inset, the menu row's own horizontal inset (shared across dropdown-menu.tsx/context-menu.tsx/menubar.tsx), and menubar.tsx's own MenubarTrigger toolbar-row inset. Counting names per value punishes exactly the values a system uses most; a primitive is a value, a semantic is a job, and a common value legitimately hosts many jobs. The cap is removed: any number of semantics may point at one primitive, without limit. What the cap was actually guarding against — a semantic that doesn't narrow anything — already has a real test, the same one that decided Finding 1 versus Finding 2 in 07e: stop and report, rather than author, if a semantic's one-line job description cannot be written without naming its own component, or if two semantics' one-line descriptions would read the same as each other. Either means the split isn't real; a numeric cap never measured that.

Re-adjudicating the four padding-8 slots and badge.tsx's own py-0.5 (2px, Finding 3, no primitive) on that test alone: the menu row's own horizontal inset survives. It is genuinely shared, proven the identical way menu-item-padding-y was — byte-identical across dropdown-menu.tsx, context-menu.tsx and menubar.tsx's own Item/CheckboxItem/RadioItem/Label/SubTrigger, not merely the same number — and its one-line job description ("a menu row's own right-edge horizontal inset, paired with either a fixed pl-8 indicator gutter or its own data-[inset] override") does not repeat any component's name and does not collide with any existing semantic's description, menu-item-padding-y's vertical counterpart included. It is authored below as menu-item-padding-x. This issue's own file scope permits editing only menubar.tsx among the three menu files, so menu-item-padding-x is wired to menubar.tsx's own Item/CheckboxItem/RadioItem/Label/SubTrigger this commit; dropdown-menu.tsx and context-menu.tsx share the identical byte-for-byte job (already established in 07e's own commit) and remain unwired only because those two files are out of this issue's scope, not because the job differs there — a future issue completes the wiring, the same incremental pattern 07c/07d/07e already used for their own out-of-scope survey files.

The other three padding-8 candidates do not survive, and not because their one-line descriptions collide with anything — each is genuinely distinguishable from every existing semantic (badge's is content-hugging with no height pairing; toggle default's is height-paired and unconditional; menubar's own MenubarTrigger inset belongs to the toolbar button itself, not a dropdown row) — but because each has exactly one consumer today. A semantic with one consumer is a value with a longer name: the type-body-strong/type-control precedent that licenses two names for one value is about two jobs that are already shared and may still diverge, not about naming a value after the single place it happens to appear right now. None of these three recurs elsewhere in src/ui today, so none is authored; all three stay raw — badge.tsx's own px-2, toggle.tsx default's own px-2, menubar.tsx's own MenubarTrigger px-2 — and this is a judgment applied on top of the description test, not a mechanical result of it, reported plainly rather than smoothed into "three more semantics" or "zero more semantics." badge.tsx's own py-0.5 fails the identical single-consumer test and stays unauthored, matching the existing one-consumer precedent already set for calendar.tsx's p-3 and command.tsx's h-12 — no padding-2 primitive is added this issue.

No renames were made. No rendered pixel changes: menu-item-padding-x points at padding-8 (8px), the exact value px-2/pr-2 already compiled to in menubar.tsx before this rewire.

Issue 07g (density — padding is done, and why): menu-item-padding-x is finished — dropdown-menu.tsx and context-menu.tsx's menu-row horizontal inset, the two files 07f left out of scope, are wired to it this commit, so the token now claims three live consumers instead of claiming three files and showing one. With that loose end closed, density's padding axis stops here, and the reason is a finding, not fatigue. Heights tokenised cleanly because "be an N-height box" is one job in every component that has it, so one name serves many. Padding mostly does not: a control's padding recipe is shaped by more than its size tier, so the same raw value lands on structurally different jobs (07e's verdict, re-proved across 07e–07f — one shared padding job found per six adjudicated slots). The rule this follows, stated so the short padding-token list below reads as deliberate rather than unfinished: a padding value shared across three or more files with the same box utility is worth a name; a value used once is a value with a longer name. The two that met it — menu-item-padding-y and menu-item-padding-x — are named and wired; nothing else in src/ui does today. R8 in scripts/check-rules.mjs (padding.shared-3-file) is the mechanism that will catch a future shared job as it appears: it requires any box-padding value reaching three files to be a decision on record — tokenised, or listed there with its category — so a new shared inset trips a review the moment it recurs, instead of hiding among the coincidences. Container padding and gaps stay raw, now permanently rather than pending: they are Tailwind's own scale showing through, not a naming job, and R8's scan confirms every container padding it flags (p-1, p-2, p-4, p-6) is a surface's own inset with no shared control job to name.

Issue 07j (elevation — the shadow axis, and a reading corrected before naming): the prompt framed this axis around a rendered inconsistency — the three menu families supposedly disagreeing about root-vs-submenu elevation, with context-menu inverted against dropdown-menu and menubar. Re-deriving the six values by COMPONENT IDENTITY rather than source-line order dissolves it: context-menu.tsx declares its SubContent before its Content, so the shadow-lg at the earlier line is the SUBMENU and the shadow-md at the later line is the ROOT — the same root=shadow-md, sub=shadow-lg every menu family uses. All three agree, and the vendored reference (shadcn new-york-v4) is identical: root=md, sub=lg across dropdown-menu, menubar and context-menu, with context-menu's SubContent likewise declared first. There is no inversion, in this port or upstream, and no rendered pixel changes this commit. Naming is by depth TIER (elevation-md, elevation-lg) rather than by menu role, for a plainer reason than an inversion: the md value is shared by popover, hover-card, navigation-menu arrow, select, combobox and the rail-sidebar panel as well as the three menu roots (nine consumers), and the lg value by alert-dialog, dialog and sheet as well as the three submenus (six consumers) — a role name like 'menu-root-shadow' would mislabel popover, so the tier is the honest shared job. The axis has four recurring jobs by consumer count (xs=16 files, sm=5, md=9, lg=6) plus one single-consumer value (xl, chart.tsx's tooltip alone — reported, not named, the one-consumer rule already set for calendar.tsx's p-3) and shadow-none used purely as a reset in seven places (input-group's three nested-control resets, combobox's nested input-group reset, sidebar's rail button, tabs' line-variant reset, toggle-group's spacing=0 reset — none is an elevation job, none wants a name; the survey said four, the true count is seven, all resets). Only elevation-md and elevation-lg are authored this commit, because only they have a real in-scope consumer on the day they land: three menu sites each. xs has one in-scope consumer (menubar's own root, shadow-xs) and a 16-file family entirely out of this issue's scope; sm has none — both are deferred to their own family commits, the same incremental rollout the control-height ladder and menu-item-padding used, and naming a tier whose family cannot be wired yet would repeat the 'value with a longer name' defect. Shadows are mode-independent: zero dark:shadow-* utilities exist in src/ui or the reference, no shadow uses an alpha that differs between light and dark, so a single value in this mode-independent file serves both — closing the plan's open dark-mode question. No rendered pixel changes: both tokens are authored as srgb black at 0.1 alpha with a unitless zero offset, byte-identical to Tailwind's own --shadow-md/--shadow-lg source strings, so they flow through the identical minifier and converge to the same #0000001a compiled form the six menu surfaces shipped before the rewire. An elevation gate is proposed but not added: an R-rule asserting any raw shadow-{md,lg} reaching three or more files must be tokenised or listed, parallel to R8's padding.shared-3-file — its claim holds for the recurring floating/elevated tiers and would correctly NOT force xs/sm/xl.

radius.$description: Base corner radius. shadcn derives the steps below from this with calc(); we author them explicitly because the values also have to be readable by tooling that has no calc().

motion-duration-base.$description: 150ms. Tailwind's --default-transition-duration, which system.css does not override — 33 transitions across 26 src/ui files run at it today, including Button's own base recipe. The most-used duration in the system by a wide margin, and the one you get without asking.

motion-duration-moderate.$description: 200ms. The most common DELIBERATE duration — 8 explicit duration-200 usages (accordion, dialog, alert-dialog, navigation-menu, sidebar, message-scroller).

motion-ease-linear.$description: Tailwind's ease-linear, four uses in src/ui.

motion-ease-in-out.$description: Tailwind's ease-in-out, read from node_modules/tailwindcss. One use in src/ui.

elevation-md.$description: Tailwind's shadow-md, authored because Issue 07j found the elevation axis has a genuine shared job at this depth tier — a floating surface that recurs across nine consumers (the three menu roots plus popover, hover-card, navigation-menu arrow, select, combobox, rail-sidebar panel). Value byte-identical to Tailwind's own --shadow-md (0 4px 6px -1px / 0 2px 4px -2px, black at 0.1 alpha), authored as srgb with a unitless zero offset so the emitted string matches Tailwind's own source and flows through the identical minifier, converging to the same #0000001a compiled form — no rendered pixel changes. Named for the tier, not a menu role, because the value is shared beyond menus: a role name like 'menu-root-shadow' would mislabel popover and select, which sit at this tier without being menu roots. (The prompt framed this axis around a supposed root-vs-sub inversion in context-menu; re-deriving by component identity shows context-menu merely declares SubContent before Content in source, and all three families — and upstream shadcn new-york-v4 — use root=md, sub=lg. No inversion, no rendered change.) Wired this commit to the md sites of the three in-scope menu files: dropdown-menu root content, menubar root content, context-menu root content. The rest of the md family keeps Tailwind's own .shadow-md unchanged and is deferred to a family commit, the same incremental pattern control-height-* and menu-item-padding-* used.

elevation-lg.$description: Tailwind's shadow-lg, the tier above elevation-md. Value byte-identical to Tailwind's own --shadow-lg (0 10px 15px -3px / 0 4px 6px -4px, black at 0.1 alpha), same srgb authoring and same #0000001a convergence — no rendered pixel changes. Named by tier like elevation-md: the lg value is shared by the three menu submenus and by alert-dialog, dialog and sheet (six consumers), so a menu-role name would mislabel the dialogs. All three menu families (and upstream) put shadow-lg on the SUBMENU and shadow-md on the root — consistent, no inversion. Wired this commit to the lg sites of the three in-scope menu files: dropdown-menu SubContent, menubar SubContent, context-menu SubContent. The rest of the lg family (alert-dialog, dialog, sheet) keeps Tailwind's own .shadow-lg unchanged and is deferred to a family commit.

leading-flush.$description: 1 — text sits flush against its box, no line-height slack. Consumers: card.tsx CardTitle, chart.tsx ChartTooltipContent row, calendar.tsx CalendarDayButton — a compact title, an inline tooltip row and a single-digit day cell, all on a size inherited from a parent.

leading-grouped.$description: 1.25 — snugs a short multi-line block so its lines read as one visual group. Consumer: attachment.tsx AttachmentContent, which stacks AttachmentTitle and AttachmentDescription on an inherited size.

leading-clustered.$description: 1.375 — keeps a field's own wrapped label or content lines clustered together, tighter than prose but not flush. Consumers: field.tsx FieldContent and FieldLabel, both on a size inherited from whatever renders inside them.

leading-prose.$description: 1.625 — comfortable reading rhythm for loose multi-line prose. Consumers: empty.tsx EmptyDescription and bubble.tsx BubbleContent, both paired with the text-body role rather than an inherited size — see each component for the role-plus-leading-override shape.

control-height-xs.$description: 24px — the xs control's fixed box height, also its icon-only square (Button size="xs"/"icon-xs", 24×24). Same raw value recurs beyond this issue's two rewired files (calendar.tsx nav button, input-group.tsx xs, rail-sidebar.tsx logo/placeholder squares), but this axis rewires only Button and Input this commit.

control-height-sm.$description: 32px — the sm control's fixed box height / icon-only square (Button size="sm"/"icon-sm"). Issue 07e wired toggle.tsx size="sm" (h-/min-w-) to this same tier — a real second consumer, not just a survey note. Also native-select.tsx data-[size=sm], sidebar.tsx menu rows, avatar.tsx default, item.tsx icon slot (still unwired).

control-height-default.$description: 36px — the default control's fixed box height / icon-only square (Button size="default"/"icon", Input's own height). Issue 07e wired menubar.tsx's own root (h-9) to this same tier. Also command.tsx input row, navigation-menu.tsx trigger, select.tsx data-[size=default], breadcrumb.tsx/pagination.tsx ellipsis squares (still unwired).

control-height-lg.$description: 40px — the lg control's fixed box height / icon-only square (Button size="lg"/"icon-lg"). Issue 07e wired toggle.tsx size="lg" (h-/min-w-) to this same tier. Also table.tsx header cell, avatar.tsx data-[size=lg], item.tsx media slot, empty.tsx icon slot (still unwired).

padding-4.$description: 4px. A primitive — named for its value, referenced only by the semantics below. Holds no opinion about who uses it; see the top-level $description's Issue 07d survey note for where 4px recurs unwired.

padding-6.$description: 6px. A primitive — named for its value, referenced only by the semantics below. Holds no opinion about who uses it; see the top-level $description's Issue 07d survey note for where 6px recurs unwired.

padding-8.$description: 8px. A primitive — named for its value, referenced only by the semantics below. Holds no opinion about who uses it; see the top-level $description's Issue 07d survey note for where 8px recurs unwired.

padding-10.$description: 10px. A primitive — named for its value, referenced only by the semantics below. Holds no opinion about who uses it; see the top-level $description's Issue 07d survey note for where 10px recurs unwired.

padding-12.$description: 12px. A primitive — named for its value, referenced only by the semantics below. Holds no opinion about who uses it; see the top-level $description's Issue 07d survey note for where 12px recurs unwired.

padding-16.$description: 16px. A primitive — named for its value, referenced only by the semantics below. Holds no opinion about who uses it; see the top-level $description's Issue 07d survey note for where 16px recurs unwired.

button-padding-x-icon-xs.$description: Button's own horizontal padding at size="xs" once it carries a leading icon (has-[>svg]:). Points at padding-6 (6px). Consumer: button.tsx size="xs".

button-padding-x-xs.$description: Button's own horizontal padding at size="xs" with no icon. Points at padding-8 (8px). Consumer: button.tsx size="xs".

button-padding-x-icon-sm.$description: Button's own horizontal padding at size="sm" once it carries a leading icon (has-[>svg]:). Points at padding-10 (10px). Consumer: button.tsx size="sm".

button-padding-x-sm.$description: Button's own horizontal padding at size="sm" with no icon. Points at padding-12 (12px) — the same primitive as input-padding-x, because the two jobs happen to share a value today, not because they are the same job. Consumer: button.tsx size="sm".

button-padding-x-default.$description: Button's own horizontal padding at size="default" with no icon, and at size="lg" once it carries a leading icon — the same 16px slot in Button's own ladder, used by two of Button's own variants, not by a foreign component. Points at padding-16 (16px). Consumers: button.tsx size="default" and size="lg" has-[>svg]:.

button-padding-y-default.$description: Button's own vertical padding at size="default". Points at padding-8 (8px). Consumer: button.tsx size="default".

input-padding-x.$description: Input's own horizontal padding — a different job from Button's sm slot even though it points at the same padding-12 primitive (12px) today. Consumer: input.tsx.

input-padding-y.$description: Input's own vertical padding, tighter than a flex-centered control needs because Input centers text by line-height, not flex. Points at padding-4 (4px). Consumer: input.tsx.

menu-item-padding-y.$description: Issue 07e. A menu's own row — Item, CheckboxItem, RadioItem, Label and SubTrigger alike — vertical padding, identical across dropdown-menu.tsx, context-menu.tsx and menubar.tsx: one genuinely shared job, not three components independently landing on the same number. Points at padding-6 (6px) — the same primitive as button-padding-x-icon-xs, because the two jobs happen to share a value today, not because they are the same job. Consumers: dropdown-menu.tsx (Item, CheckboxItem, RadioItem, Label, SubTrigger), context-menu.tsx (Item, CheckboxItem, RadioItem, Label, SubTrigger), menubar.tsx (MenubarItem, MenubarCheckboxItem, MenubarRadioItem, MenubarLabel, MenubarSubTrigger).

menu-item-padding-x.$description: Issue 07f. A menu row's own right-edge horizontal inset — paired with either a fixed pl-8 indicator gutter (CheckboxItem, RadioItem) or its own data-[inset] override (Item, Label, SubTrigger) — the horizontal counterpart to menu-item-padding-y, surviving the same test that padding-8's other three candidates failed: it recurs byte-identical across dropdown-menu.tsx, context-menu.tsx and menubar.tsx, not merely at the same number. Points at padding-8 (8px) — the same primitive as button-padding-x-xs/button-padding-y-default, because the jobs happen to share a value today, not because they are the same job; no per-primitive cap applies (see this file's own Issue 07f paragraph). Issue 07g wired the two files 07f left out of scope, so all three menu files are now live consumers. Consumers: menubar.tsx, dropdown-menu.tsx, context-menu.tsx (each: Item, CheckboxItem, RadioItem, Label, SubTrigger).

toggle-padding-x-lg.$description: Issue 07e. Toggle's own horizontal padding at size="lg" — unconditional (not has-[>svg]:-gated the way Button's own icon compound is) and paired with Toggle's own 40px height. Points at padding-10 (10px) — the same primitive as button-padding-x-icon-sm, because the two jobs happen to share a value today, not because they are the same job. Consumer: toggle.tsx size="lg".

kbd-padding-x.$description: Issue 07e. Kbd's own horizontal padding around its glyph — a different CSS axis from input-padding-y's vertical job even though both point at padding-4 (4px) today. Consumer: kbd.tsx.

type-display.$description: Largest heading, for documentation surfaces — hero titles, landing-page headers.

type-heading-lg.$description: Largest in-app heading — page titles, top-level section headers.

type-heading.$description: Section heading — dialog titles, card titles, sub-sections.

type-heading-sm.$description: Small heading — nested sections, sidebar group titles. Line height equals font size: it sits on a single tight line, not a flowing paragraph. Tracking is normal because no src/ui title ships a tracking utility; the -0.025em on the unconsumed heading roles is the authored ideal, and collapsing the two is a deliberate change with its own commit.

type-heading-sm-loose.$description: 18px title on a normal line box — AlertDialog and Empty titles. type-heading-sm is the leading-none variant Dialog ships; these two are not the same value and are not being merged in this issue. Tracking is normal because no src/ui title ships a tracking utility; the -0.025em on the unconsumed heading roles is the authored ideal, and collapsing the two is a deliberate change with its own commit.

type-body-lg.$description: Larger body copy — lead paragraphs, empty-state descriptions.

type-body.$description: Default running text — paragraphs, descriptions, list items.

type-body-strong.$description: Emphasised inline text within body copy — same metrics as type-body, heavier weight.

type-control.$description: Button, input, tab and menu item label. 20px line height, matching the shipped text-sm control metrics.

type-control-sm.$description: Small control and micro-label — Kbd, Badge emphasis, sidebar group labels, message authors, combobox chips. 12px at weight 500, the most repeated recipe after type-control.

type-caption.$description: Secondary/supporting text — helper text, timestamps, metadata.

type-label.$description: Form field label — matches the Label component's shipped metrics (text-sm, leading-none, weight 500).

type-eyebrow.$description: Uppercase micro-label — section eyebrows, sidebar category headings. Not the Label component; form labels use type-label. Site and documentation surfaces only; no src/ui component consumes this. Do not wire a component to it — components use type-control-sm.

type-metric.$description: Large numeric statistic, for documentation surfaces — dashboards, stat cards. Tabular figures so digits don't shift width.

type-metric-sm.$description: Smaller numeric statistic — compact stat cards, inline metrics. Tabular figures so digits don't shift width.

type-code.$description: Inline and block code — monospace body text.

type-shortcut.$description: Keyboard shortcut hint in a menu — DropdownMenu, ContextMenu, Menubar, Command. Weight 400 with wide tracking, which is why it is not type-control-sm.
